name: Buxa Fort & Buxa Tiger Reserve
description: Spanning 760 square kilometers in the Buxa Hills along the international border with Bhutan, a vital trans-boundary elephant and tiger corridor encompassing dense sal forests, home to the historic Buxa Fort perched at 2,870 feet where the British imprisoned prominent Indian freedom fighters including Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and revolutionary freedom fighters in the 1930s.

name: Chilapata Forest & Nalrajar Garh
description: Spanning dense sub-tropical terai forest between Jaldapara National Park and Buxa Tiger Reserve, celebrated as the primary ecological migration corridor for wild Asian elephants and Indian one-horned rhinoceroses, famous for the 'Ram Gumo' (bleeding tree) and the ancient ruins of Nalrajar Garh, a 5th-century CE Gupta-period brick fortress hidden deep inside the jungle.

name: Jaldapara National Park
description: Situated in the Eastern Dooars foothills along the Torsa River, a 216-square-kilometer national park holding the second largest population of Indian One-Horned Rhinoceroses in India after Kaziranga, set amidst lush tall elephant grass and riverine forests.

name: Jayanti Riverbed & Mahakal Caves
description: Referred to affectionately as the 'Queen of Dooars', an enchanting forest village situated on the banks of the Jayanti River forming a natural border with Bhutan, famous for its dry white pebble-strewn riverbed framed by towering green hills, and a thrilling 15-km forest trek leading to the sacred Jayanti Mahakal stalactite and stalagmite limestone caves dedicated to Lord Shiva.

name: Lepchakha Village & Rovers Point Buxa
description: Perched at an elevation of nearly 3,000 feet atop a secluded hill plateau inside the Buxa Tiger Reserve 5 km beyond Buxa Fort near the Bhutan border, an enchanting mountain village inhabited by the Drukpa Buddhist community, famous for its small hilltop gompa, Rovers Point (the 'Hill of Thirty Hills'), and an awe-inspiring panoramic view of 12 glistening rivers meandering through the plains of Bengal and Bhutan.

name: Madarihat & Jaldapara Safari Gateway
description: Situated along National Highway 31C on the northern fringe of Jaldapara National Park 50 km from Alipurduar, celebrated as the primary safari booking headquarters, hotel hub, and tourist base for exploring Jaldapara, featuring the iconic Jaldapara Tourist Lodge (Hollong Lodge safari base), forest department elephant-riding corrals, and vibrant Dooars tribal handicraft markets.

name: Rajabhatkhawa Vulture Conservation Centre & Gate
description: Situated 15 km north of Alipurduar at the forested entrance to the Buxa Tiger Reserve, celebrated as the primary forest entry gateway and safari permit hub for Buxa, famous for the specialized Vulture Conservation Breeding Centre (VCBC) established by the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) and West Bengal Forest Department to breed and reintroduce critically endangered Oriental White-backed and Slender-billed vultures, and a wildlife rescue facility.

name: South Khairbari Leopard & Tiger Rescue Centre
description: Situated 10 km from Madarihat in the Dooars forest belt, celebrated as the first and only specialized animal rehabilitation and rescue center in South Asia dedicated to the scientific care of Royal Bengal tigers and Indian leopards rescued from illegal circuses, animal abuse, and human-wildlife conflict zones, featuring expansive semi-natural forested enclosures, a battery-car safari, and a scenic boathouse on the Buri Torsa River.

name: Totopara Tribal Village Alipurduar
description: Situated on the banks of the Titi River along the foothills of the Bhutan border 22 km from Madarihat, celebrated as the exclusive ancestral home of the Toto tribe—one of the world's smallest and most isolated indigenous ethnic groups comprising fewer than 1,600 living members, featuring traditional bamboo-and-thatch stilt houses ('Chha'), terraced betel-nut groves, and rich oral traditions.

name: Biharinath Hill (Highest Peak in Bankura)
description: Rising to 1,480 feet (451 meters) amidst the pristine sal, mahua, and palash woodlands in Saltora block along the Damodar River basin, celebrated as the highest mountain summit in Bankura district, known as the 'Aravalli of Bengal', featuring an adventurous rocky trekking trail through dense forests, natural perennial freshwater hill springs, and the ancient Biharinath Shiva Temple at the mountain base.

name: Bishnupur Temples
description: Nestled in the picturesque town of Bishnupur, West Bengal, lies a treasure trove of spiritual and cultural heritage – the Bishnupur Temples. This village, often referred to as 'Narayangarh,' boasts a majestic collection of 15th to 18th-century temples, each a masterpiece of Bengali architecture. Adorned with vibrant terracotta decorations and intricate carvings, these ancient temples showcase the artistic brilliance of the Sadgop community, once renowned for their skills in pottery and temple construction. Visitors can immerse themselves in the tranquil atmosphere, taking in the rich history and breathtaking beauty of these sacred structures.

name: Dalmadal Cannon Bishnupur
description: Forged in the 18th century under Malla King Gopal Singh using 63 individual wrought iron rings welded together with charcoal heat, a colossal historical cannon measuring 3.8 meters (12.5 feet) in length with a barrel diameter of 28.5 cm, celebrated in Bengal folklore as 'Dalmadal' (Destroyer of Hordes) which miraculously did not rust despite being exposed to monsoon rains for over 250 years.

name: Gorasankar Dual Temples Dihar Bankura
description: Situated in Dihar village along the Kana Damodar River 8 km north of Bishnupur, an internationally celebrated archaeological and architectural site featuring twin 11th-century CE laterite stone rekha-deul temples dedicated to Lord Shiva as Sareswar and Saileswar (collectively Gorasankar), renowned for being the oldest surviving standing stone temples in the Bishnupur region, decorated with exquisite floral friezes, miniature chaitya gavakshas, and stone animal reliefs.

name: Jhilimili & Ranibandh Forest Rim Bankura
description: Situated in Ranibandh block 70 km southwest of Bankura near the border with Purulia and Jhargram, an enchanting wilderness destination known as 'Jhilimili' (literally 'Sparkling Rim'), situated on a high laterite ridge covered in dense, pristine Sal, Mahua, and Kusum forests, offering dramatic panoramic views down into the misty gorge of the Kangsabati River from elevated forest watchtowers.

name: Jor Bangla Temple (Keshta Raya) Bishnupur
description: Constructed in 1655 CE by Malla King Raghunath Singh, acknowledged globally as the absolute pinnacle of Bengal terracotta temple art, built in the traditional 'Yor-Bangla' (twin hut) style joining two curved thatched-roof do-chala structures with a central char-chala tower, featuring walls entirely blanketed with hyper-detailed terracotta relief plaques depicting the Ramayana, Mahabharata, royal hunts, and maritime boats.

name: Joypur Forest & British Watchtower Bankura
description: Covering 120 square kilometers of dense Sal, Kusum, and Teak woodland 14 km east of Bishnupur along the state highway, celebrated as one of southern Bengal's richest deciduous forest reserves, home to free-roaming herds of wild Spotted Deer (Chital), wild boars, peacocks, and seasonal migratory elephant herds from Dalma, featuring an elevated historic British-era watchtower overlooking a forest clearing and watering hole.

name: Joyrambati Matri Mandir Bankura
description: Situated in Joyrambati village in Bankura district 5 km from Kamarpukur, revered as the holy birthplace of Holy Mother Sri Sarada Devi (1853-1920), spiritual consort of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and universal mother of the Ramakrishna Order, featuring the tranquil white marble Matri Mandir consecrated in 1923 enshrining a marble deity of Holy Mother over her exact birthplace, alongside her preserved ancestral thatched mud cottage.

name: Kalachand Temple Bishnupur
description: Constructed in 1656 CE by Malla King Raghunath Singha on an elevated square plinth in southern Bishnupur, an imposing laterite stone temple designed in the classic eka-ratna architectural style, crowned by a single curvilinear shikhara, world-famous for its well-preserved laterite relief bas-reliefs illustrating dynamic battle scenes from the Mahabharata, royal hunts, and Krishna Leela pastimes.

name: Lalji Temple Bishnupur
description: Constructed in 1658 CE by Malla King Bir Singha II, situated on a high square laterite plinth within an enclosed fortified compound in Bishnupur, dedicated to Radhika and Krishna as Lalji, featuring an impressive eka-ratna shikhara topped by an amalaka and kalasa, an ornamental dancing hall (Natmandir) in front, and exquisite laterite bas-relief carvings depicting Puranic legends and royal court scenes.

name: Maa Mrinmoyee Temple Bishnupur
description: Established in 997 CE by King Jagat Malla when he shifted the Malla capital to Bishnupur, celebrated as the oldest standing and continuously active temple in Bishnupur, enshrining an ancient clay and stone deity of Maa Durga known as 'Mrinmoyee' ('Made of Clay'), famed for its monumental 1,025-year-old royal Durga Puja tradition where the firing of the Dalmadal cannon historically announced the start of Mahashtami sandhi puja.

name: Madan Mohan Temple Bishnupur
description: Built in 1694 CE by Malla King Durjana Singh Deva in the eka-ratna (single-pinnacled) style, celebrated as one of the few historic temples in Bishnupur where active worship continues to this day, featuring fine terracotta relief plaques depicting Krishna dancing and kirtan processions, historically famous as the abode of the presiding deity Madan Mohan who legend says personally fired the Dalmadal cannon to repel Maratha Bargi invaders.

name: Mukutmanipur
description: Mukutmanipur, nestled in the Bankura district of West Bengal, is a treasure trove of natural wonders. The destination boasts a remarkable confluence of the Kangsabati and Kumari rivers, creating a breathtaking landscape that is dotted with rugged hills and verdant forests. The region is steeped in history, with remnants of the past visible in its ancient temples and artifacts. As a visitor, one can immerse themselves in the serene atmosphere, engage with the warm locals, and indulge in a plethora of activities that cater to various interests, from nature walks and photography to bird watching and local sightseeing. The unique blend of natural beauty, cultural heritage, and warm hospitality makes Mukutmanipur an idyllic getaway for those seeking a tranquil retreat from the chaos of urban life.

name: Panchmura Terracotta Village Bankura
description: Situated in Taldangra block 21 km from Bishnupur, a world-famous craft heritage village where over 300 traditional Kumbhakar (potter) families have practiced terracotta pottery for generations, celebrated internationally as the birthplace of the GI-tagged Bankura Terracotta Horse (featuring erect ears, arched neck, and hollow earthenware construction) which serves as the official national logo of All India Handicrafts.

name: Radha Gobinda Temple Bishnupur
description: Constructed in 1729 CE during the reign of Malla King Gopal Singha by Krishna Singha, a graceful laterite stone eka-ratna temple situated near the Kalachand temple in Bishnupur, featuring an ornamental pyramidal shikhara, a unique small miniature stone chariot (Rath) within the courtyard, and exquisite geometric and floral laterite stone carvings.

name: Radha Shyam Temple Bishnupur
description: Constructed in 1758 CE by Malla King Chaitanya Singha inside the fortified inner citadel of Bishnupur, an imposing eka-ratna style temple built of fine laterite stone rather than brick, rising on a square plinth with a curvilinear shikhara, world-famous for its well-preserved, delicate white lime-stucco relief carvings depicting Lord Krishna with gopis, scenes from the Puranas, floral medallions, and geometric borders.

name: Rasmancha Bishnupur
description: Commissioned in 1600 CE by Malla King Bir Hambir in the temple town of Bishnupur, an architectural monument unique in the entire world resembling an Egyptian stepped pyramid, constructed on a high square laterite plinth rising 12.5 meters with a pyramidical brick superstructure encircled by three concentric galleries of 108 arched passageways, designed historically to display all Radha-Krishna idols from across the kingdom during the annual Ras festival.

name: Shyam Rai Temple Bishnupur
description: Constructed in 1643 CE by King Raghunath Singh, celebrated as the earliest and finest pancha-ratna (five-towered) terracotta temple in Bengal, adorned on all four exterior and interior walls with museum-grade terracotta carvings, world-famous for its central circular terracotta ceiling medallion depicting Lord Krishna dancing with gopis in the divine Raslila surrounded by floral geometry.

name: Susunia Hill & 4th-Century Inscription
description: Rising 1,442 feet (440 meters) amidst the flat alluvial plains of Bankura district, an ancient isolated granite hill celebrated as a premier archaeological and rock-climbing destination, featuring the oldest rock inscription in West Bengal (dating to the 4th century CE under King Chandravarman carved with a fiery disc chakra), natural perennial mineral springs, and artisan hamlets at the base famous for stone-carving crafts.

name: Sutan Forest & Ranibandh Lake Bankura
description: Nestled in the deep forested hills of Ranibandh block 60 km southwest of Bankura town, celebrated as one of Bengal's most pristine virgin sal forest wildernesses, spanning thousands of acres of dense Sal, Mahua, and Kendu trees, centered around the tranquil, secluded Sutan Lake with its elevated forest watchtower, where wild elephant herds, barking deer, and wild boars roam along natural forest corridors.

name: Amar Kutir Craft Society Santiniketan
description: Founded in 1927 on the banks of the Kopai River by revolutionary freedom fighter Sushen Mukherjee as a political refuge for freedom fighters running underground printing presses, transformed in 1948 into a pioneering village craft cooperative society, celebrated internationally for reviving rural handicrafts including the official GI-tagged 'Santiniketan Embossed Leather Goods', Kantha embroidery, batik textiles, and Dokra metal casting.

name: Bakreswar Thermal Hot Springs & Shiva Temple
description: Situated 18 km southwest of Suri along the Bakreswar River, an extraordinary geological and spiritual destination featuring a cluster of eight natural perennial thermal sulphur springs with temperatures ranging from 44°C to an astonishing 72°C in the Agnikunda spring (reputed to be the hottest spring in eastern India), discharging helium gas with therapeutic properties for skin diseases, alongside the ancient Bakreswar Shiva Temple and Mahishamardini Shakti Peetha.

name: Ballavpur Wildlife Sanctuary Santiniketan
description: Established in 1977 across 200 hectares of undulating laterite soil covered in lush sal, akashmoni, and eucalyptus woodlands near Visva-Bharati in Santiniketan, widely known as the 'Deer Park', celebrated for its thriving breeding population of hundreds of free-roaming Spotted Deer (Chital) and Blackbuck antelopes, alongside three large natural wetlands that attract thousands of winter migratory ducks and teal.

name: Fullara Shakti Peetha Labhpur
description: Situated 30 km from Bolpur-Santiniketan on the banks of the Kopai River in Labhpur, revered as one of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where Goddess Sati's lower lip fell, enshrining an aniconic red stone deity, celebrated for the adjacent sacred pond 'Daldali' where according to Hindu legend Lord Rama collected 108 blue lotuses for his autumn Durga Puja, deeply woven into novelist Tarasankar Bandyopadhyay's epic literature.

name: Jaydev Kenduli & Baul Mela (Ajay River)
description: Situated on the peaceful banks of the sacred Ajay River 30 km from Bolpur, revered as the historic 12th-century birthplace of legendary Sanskrit poet Jayadeva, court poet of King Lakshmana Sena and composer of the immortal devotional lyric 'Gita Govinda', featuring the 1683 CE terracotta Radhabinod Temple built by the Queen of Burdwan, and host to the world-famous Kenduli Baul Mela every Makar Sankranti (mid-January) where hundreds of mystic wandering Baul and Fakir minstrels assemble in akharas.

name: Kala Bhavana & Black House Visva-Bharati
description: Founded in 1919 by Rabindranath Tagore at Visva-Bharati with legendary master artist Nandalal Bose as its first principal, recognized globally as the cradle of modern Indian art, featuring open-air studios, the iconic 'Black House' (Kalo Bari - a mud-and-tar student hostel ornamented with monumental relief sculptures designed by Nandalal Bose and master sculptor Ramkinkar Baij), and monumental outdoor open-air sculptures including 'Santhal Family' and 'Mill Call'.

name: Kankalitala Shakti Peetha Bolpur
description: Situated on the peaceful banks of the Kopai River 9 km from Bolpur in Birbhum district, revered as one of the most sacred of the 51 Shakti Peethas where the waist (Kankal / pelvis) of Goddess Sati fell, featuring a serene temple complex without an idol, where the divine relic is worshiped inside a sacred subterranean water tank (Kundupukur), alongside an active cremation ground and sacred banyan trees.

name: Kopai River & Sonajhurir Haat Santiniketan
description: Situated along the red laterite gullies (Khowai) of the meandering Kopai River on the northern edge of Santiniketan, immortalized in Rabindranath Tagore's beloved childhood poem 'Amader Chhoto Nodi Chale Bānke Bānke', world-famous for the vibrant Saturday 'Sonajhurir Haat' (Shonajhuri Open-Air Tribal Market) held under golden acacia trees, where hundreds of local Santhal women and village artisans sell handloom Kantha-stitch sarees, Dokra jewelry, and handmade leather bags while Baul bards sing live under the trees.

name: Massanjore Dam & Mayurakshi Reservoir
description: Constructed in 1955 across the Mayurakshi River near the border of Birbhum district 35 km from Suri, built with Canadian foreign assistance under the Colombo Plan and formally known as 'Canada Dam', celebrated as one of the most scenic reservoir destinations in eastern India, spanning 2,170 feet across the river, holding a vast 16,000-acre sapphire reservoir framed by rolling green forested hillocks, offering speed boating, pedal boating, and hillside viewpoints.

name: Nalateswari Temple Nalhati
description: Perched upon a small forested hillock (Nalhati Hill) 15 km from Rampurhat in northern Birbhum, celebrated as one of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where Goddess Sati's vocal cord or throat (Nala) fell, giving the town its name Nalhati, enshrining a golden-faced deity of Goddess Nalateswari (a form of Kali) with a tongue extending outward, alongside natural perennial hill springs and the shrine of Bhairava Yogesh.

name: Nandikeshwari Temple Sainthia
description: Situated on the banks of the Mayurakshi River in the commercial town of Sainthia in Birbhum district, celebrated as one of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where Goddess Sati's divine necklace (Haar) fell, enshrining an ancient, formless natural rock deity coated in sacred vermilion resembling the back of a tortoise, sheltered beneath a colossal, century-old sacred banyan tree draped in red prayer ribbons.

name: Rabindra Bhavana & Museum Santiniketan
description: Established in 1942 inside the historic Uttarayan complex at Visva-Bharati in Santiniketan, recognized as the premier research institute and memorial museum dedicated to the life and works of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore, housing his original Nobel Prize diploma and medal replicas, over 1,500 original paintings and sketches, original handwritten drafts of 'Gitanjali', his vintage Humber car, and gifts presented by world leaders.

name: Sonajhuri Forest & Khoai Haat Santiniketan
description: Situated on the banks of the Kopai River on unique wind-eroded red-soil ravines known as 'Khoai', an enchanting forest of slender yellow-flowering Sonajhuri trees, celebrated across India for the vibrant weekly outdoor artisan market 'Shanibarer Khoai Haat' (Saturday Haat), where hundreds of Santhal tribal artisans, kantha-stitch embroiderers, dokra metal casters, and singing Baul folk minstrels assemble under the trees.

name: Sriniketan Rural Reconstruction Institute
description: Founded on 6 February 1922 by Rabindranath Tagore in collaboration with English agricultural economist Leonard Elmhirst at Surul 3 km west of Santiniketan, established as Tagore's pioneering laboratory for rural reconstruction, sustainable agriculture, and village self-reliance, featuring the historic 'Kuthi Bari' (Surul Kuthi), the Silpa Sadana artisan training workshops for leathercraft, batik, and pottery, and the annual Sriniketan Magh Mela.

name: Tarapith Temple Birbhum
description: Situated on the banks of the sacred Dwarka River 9 km from Rampurhat in Birbhum district, celebrated across India as one of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where Sati's third eye (Tara) fell, and the paramount center of Tantric Shakta worship, housing a fiercely loving silver-faced idol of Goddess Tara suckling Lord Shiva as an infant, immortalized by the 19th-century saint Bama Khepa who meditated in the adjacent sacred Mahasmashan cremation ground.

name: Upasana Griha & Chatimtala Santiniketan
description: Situated in the core heritage precinct of Visva-Bharati in Santiniketan, comprising Chatimtala (the sacred open-air grove of Chatim trees where Maharshi Debendranath Tagore experienced spiritual revelation in 1863, inscribed with 'He is the solace of my life, the joy of my mind, the peace of my soul'), and the adjacent Upasana Griha (consecrated in 1891, an exquisite Belgian stained-glass non-denominational Prayer Hall illuminated with hundreds of candles on Wednesday mornings).

name: Visva-Bharati & Uttarayan Complex Santiniketan
description: Established in 1901 by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore as an experimental open-air residential school under shaded mango and sal groves, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in September 2023, comprising the historic Uttarayan Complex with Tagore's five distinct architectural residences (Udayan, Konarka, Shyamali, Punascha, and Udichi), the Rabindra Bhavana archives museum, Kala Bhavana (fine arts), and Upasana Griha (Belgium stained-glass prayer hall).

name: Baneswar Shiva Temple Cooch Behar
description: Constructed in the 16th century by Maharaja Nara Narayan of the Koch dynasty 12 km north of Cooch Behar town, an ancient terracotta brick temple enshrining a self-manifested Shiva lingam, celebrated worldwide for its adjacent sacred temple pond (Shibbari Pukur) which provides a protected community sanctuary for hundreds of critically endangered Black Softshell Turtles (Nilssonia nigricans), known locally as 'Mohan', which respond to the priests' calls to eat puffed rice.

name: Baradebi Temple Cooch Behar
description: Situated in the Debibari royal temple complex of Cooch Behar town, the ancestral state shrine of the Koch royal dynasty dedicated to Goddess Baradebi (a colossal, ferocious clay manifestation of Goddess Durga accompanied by tiger, lion, Jaya, and Bijaya), constructed during the reign of Maharaja Biswa Singha and Maharaja Nara Narayana in the 16th century, celebrated for its unique 500-year-old royal Durga Puja rituals including midnight royal sacrifices and clay idol immersion.

name: Cooch Behar Palace (Victor Jubilee Palace)
description: Constructed in 1887 under Maharaja Nripendra Narayan, an opulent double-storeyed palace covering over 51,000 square feet, designed in the classical Italian Renaissance style modeled on London's Buckingham Palace, featuring an imposing Corinthian-domed central rotunda.

name: Gosanimari Rajpat & Kamtapur Ruins
description: Situated in Dinhata subdivision 35 km south of Cooch Behar on the Dharla River basin, celebrated as the monumental archaeological capital of the medieval Kamtapur kingdom that ruled northern Bengal and Assam between the 11th and 15th centuries CE under the Khen dynasty, featuring colossal excavated brick ramparts, royal palace foundations, deep defensive moats, ancient stone wells, and intricately carved chlorite stone sculptures.

name: Kamteswari Temple Dinhata Cooch Behar
description: Situated in Gosanimari near Dinhata 35 km from Cooch Behar town along the Singimari River, celebrated as one of North Bengal's oldest and most venerated Shakti shrines, originally founded by the medieval Kamta kings and reconstructed in 1665 CE by Maharaja Pran Narayan of Cooch Behar, enshrining Goddess Kamteswari (a form of Goddess Chandi as the tutelary guardian of the Kamtapur realm) upon a square brick sanctum with arched gateways.

name: Madan Mohan Temple Cooch Behar
description: Constructed between 1885 and 1889 CE by Maharaja Nripendra Narayan in the center of Cooch Behar town, celebrated as the supreme spiritual sanctuary of the Koch dynasty, enshrining the family deity Lord Madan Mohan alongside deities of Goddess Kali, Tara, and Bhavani, host to the legendary 200-year-old Cooch Behar Rash Mela (the oldest and largest traditional fair in North Bengal) centered around the spinning of the monumental sacred wooden Rash Chakra.

name: Rasik Beel Wetland & Bird Sanctuary
description: Covering 178 hectares around a series of interconnected oxbow lakes and perennial marshes in Tufanganj subdivision 42 km from Cooch Behar town, a premier wetland sanctuary in northern Bengal hosting over 170 species of resident and migratory waterbirds, featuring a 70-foot watchtower, a dedicated Gharial and tortoise breeding pond, a deer rehabilitation park, and an aquarium.

name: Bolla Kali Temple Balurghat Dakshin Dinajpur
description: Situated in Bolla village along the Balurghat-Malda highway 15 km from Balurghat on the Punarbhaba River basin, celebrated as the supreme spiritual sanctuary of Dakshin Dinajpur, dedicated to Goddess Kali as Bolla Ma, whose divine legend dates back to a captive local landlord who prayed for freedom from the East India Company and was miraculously released, host to the legendary 4-day Bolla Kali Mela held the Friday after Rash Purnima attracting over 1 million devotees.

name: Buniadpur Municipal Eco-Park & Wetland
description: Sprawling across 25 landscaped acres in the modern municipal township of Buniadpur 45 km west of Balurghat in Dakshin Dinajpur district, developed as a premier recreational urban eco-park and water recreation destination, centered around an expansive natural freshwater lake equipped with pedal boating, illuminated musical fountains, landscaped flower gardens, open-air amphitheatres, and children's amusement joy rides.

name: Gangarampur (Bangarh Archaeological Site)
description: Situated along the Punarbhaba River in Gangarampur subdivision 45 km from Balurghat, celebrated as one of the most prominent excavated ancient historical fortified cities in Bengal, known in classical Sanskrit texts as 'Kotivarsa' (capital of the Kotivarsa vishaya in the Gupta empire), revealing continuous cultural strata spanning from the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE) through Sunga, Kushana, Gupta, and Pala empires, featuring massive brick ramparts, moats, and the 11th-century carved stone pillar of King Nayapala.

name: Kali Dighi & Dhal Dighi Gangarampur
description: Situated in Gangarampur subdivision 40 km from Balurghat in Dakshin Dinajpur, a pair of colossal historic man-made rectangular lakes excavated between the 10th and 11th centuries CE during the Pala dynasty—Kali Dighi (named after Goddess Kali, spanning 1.5 km in length) and Dhal Dighi (White Lake, spanning 1.2 km in length), surrounded by ancient archaeological brick mounds, ancient lotus groves, and serving as vital winter waterfowl stopovers.

name: Patiram Archaeological Mounds & Atrai River
description: Situated on the fertile banks of the Atrai River 12 km north of Balurghat in Dakshin Dinajpur district, celebrated as a historic medieval trading post and ancient archaeological site dating back to the Pala and Sena dynasties, famous for large ancient royal freshwater reservoirs (Dighis), ancient brick temple mounds, traditional handloom silk weaving cottage units, and peaceful river ghats.

name: Tapan Dighi Historic Lake Balurghat
description: Situated in Tapan block 35 km northwest of Balurghat in Dakshin Dinajpur, an immense 2-kilometer-long man-made freshwater reservoir measuring 2,000 meters by 800 meters excavated in the 12th century CE under King Lakshmana Sena of the Sena dynasty, surrounded by ancient archaeological mounds, laterite temples, and sprawling tree-lined banks that host thousands of winter migratory waterfowl.

name: Ambootia Bio-Dynamic Organic Tea Estate Kurseong
description: Established in 1861 on the southern slopes of the Kurseong ridge at altitudes from 3,200 to 4,500 feet overlooking the Balasun river basin, celebrated globally as a pioneer in bio-dynamic and 100% organic tea cultivation, spanning 400 hectares with over 1,000 plantation workers, renowned for producing exquisite, award-winning floral first-flush and Muscatel second-flush black teas exported to gourmet tea salons in Paris, Berlin, and Tokyo.

name: Balasun Tea Estate Kurseong
description: Established in 1871 by British planters across 440 hectares along the rolling slopes of the Balasun River valley near Panighatta 15 km from Kurseong, celebrated for its diverse topography ranging from 1,200 to 4,500 feet, famous for producing full-bodied, golden-orange orthodox black teas and whole-leaf flowery orange pekoes with sweet woody aromas, surrounded by mountain streams and orange orchards.

name: Batasia Loop & Gorkha War Memorial
description: Engineered in 1919 by the British on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway line 5 km below Darjeeling, a brilliant 360-degree railway spiral loop where the Toy Train wraps around itself through landscaped garden terraces to negotiate a steep 140-foot descent, featuring the central Gorkha War Memorial with a bronze statue of an Indian soldier paying tribute to Gorkha martyrs.

name: Bengal Natural History Museum Darjeeling
description: Originally founded in 1903 as a modest butterfly and bird collection under British Lt. Governor Sir John Woodburn on the grounds of the Botanical Garden and relocated near Chowrasta, an extraordinary natural history museum housing over 4,300 authentic preserved specimens of Himalayan wildlife, including Bengal tigers, snow leopards, Himalayan black bears, over 800 species of regional birds, reptiles, and vibrant montane insects.

name: Castleton Tea Estate Kurseong
description: Established in 1885 by Dr. Charles Graham across 170 hectares in the Pankhabari valley near Kurseong at elevations from 3,200 to 7,500 feet, celebrated globally by tea connoisseurs as the 'Champagne of Teas', holding multiple international auction world records for fetching the highest prices ever paid for pure orthodox black tea, famous for its sweet, lingering Muscatel grape aroma harvested from pure China-variety bushes.

name: Chamong Tea Estate & Luxury Resort
description: Established in 1871 in the Rongbong Valley near Pokhriabong at altitudes ranging from 3,800 to 6,000 feet, celebrated as a flagship 100% certified organic and bio-dynamic tea estate spanning 330 hectares, renowned for producing fragrant floral Darjeeling green and white teas, featuring the luxury Chamong Chiabari tea retreat with panoramic glass villas, private nature walks, and tea-blending workshops.

name: Chatakpur Eco Village Senchal
description: Nestled inside the dense pine and oak canopy of the Senchal Wildlife Sanctuary at an altitude of 7,887 feet, an exceptionally pristine eco-village consisting of only 18 organic farming households, developed by the West Bengal Forest Department to curb timber smuggling through sustainable eco-tourism, famous for its wooden watchtower offering 180-degree unobstructed panoramas of Mount Kanchenjunga.

name: Chitrey Mountain Hamlet & Monastery
description: Perched at an elevation of 8,340 feet (2,542 meters) along a steep 3-km uphill trail from Manebhanjan, an atmospheric mountain hamlet on the Singalila Ridge trek, famous for the serene Chitrey Buddhist Monastery adorned with colorful prayer flags, panoramic vantage points overlooking the rolling hills of Darjeeling and Kurseong, and a peaceful resting meadow for trekkers and vintage Land Rovers.

name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway / Toy Train (UNESCO)
description: Constructed between 1879 and 1881, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1999, an astonishing 88-kilometer 2-foot (610 mm) narrow-gauge railway climbing from New Jalpaiguri at 100 meters above sea level to Ghum (India's highest railway station at 2,258 m) before descending to Darjeeling, using innovative zigzag reversals and spiral loops powered by vintage 19th-century British 'B-Class' steam locomotives.

name: Darjeeling Mall & Chowrasta
description: Perched on the crest of a ridge at 7,000 feet in the heart of Darjeeling, the historic commercial and cultural public square known as Chowrasta (where four roads meet), a car-free pedestrian haven lined with heritage Victorian park benches, pine trees, pony rides, century-old bakeries, and the statue of Nepali poet Bhanubhakta Acharya, offering sweeping views of Mount Kanchenjunga.

name: Darjeeling Ropeway (Rangeet Valley Cable Car)
description: Originally established in 1968 at North Point (Singamari) in Darjeeling at an altitude of 7,000 feet, celebrated as the first passenger ropeway in India, gliding gracefully over the deep, emerald tea estates of the Rangeet River valley down to Tukvar station at 2,500 feet across a cable span of 5 kilometers, offering passengers breathtaking aerial vistas of rolling tea slopes, waterfalls, and Mount Kanchenjunga.

name: Ghum Railway Station & DHR Toy Train Museum
description: Perched at an altitude of 7,407 feet (2,258 meters) on the mountain ridge 6 km before Darjeeling, recognized as the highest railway station in India and the 14th highest in the world, serving the UNESCO World Heritage Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, featuring the official DHR Railway Museum established inside the heritage station building displaying vintage steam locomotive models, historical station clocks, railway lanterns, and the prized 1881 vintage 'Baby Sivok' B-class steam locomotive.

name: Ging Tea House & Heritage Estate
description: Established in 1864 in the picturesque Lebong Valley 10 km below Darjeeling town, one of the earliest commercial tea plantations in the region, featuring a restored Victorian planter's bungalow with polished teak flooring, stone fireplaces, wraparound verandas, billiard rooms, and lush tea trails overlooking the snow-crested Himalayas.

name: Glenburn Tea Estate Darjeeling
description: Established in 1859 by Scottish tea planters across 1,600 acres of rolling green hills in the Takdah valley, celebrated as one of India's most luxurious and picturesque tea heritage retreats, featuring two restored colonial planter bungalows with fireplace suites, private river campsites along the River Rungeet, rolling orthodox organic tea plantations, and guided tea-tasting sessions.

name: Goomtee Tea Estate & Waterfall Kurseong
description: Established in 1899 near Kurseong along the historic Hill Cart Road at an altitude of 4,500 feet, celebrated for producing internationally award-winning Muscatel Darjeeling teas, featuring a charming century-old heritage bungalow, cascading mountain waterfalls running through the tea garden, and guided plucking tours.

name: Happy Valley Tea Estate Darjeeling
description: Established in 1854 by David Wilson as Wilson Tea Estate across 437 rolling acres just 3 km below Darjeeling town at an elevation of 6,800 feet, celebrated as the second oldest tea estate in the Darjeeling district, producing world-renowned organic orthodox black, green, and white teas, featuring an active vintage processing factory with guided tea tasting tours.

name: Himalayan Mountaineering Institute & Museum (HMI)
description: Established on 4 November 1954 by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Everest pioneer Tenzing Norgay on Birch Hill, one of the world's foremost mountaineering training institutes, featuring a world-class Mountaineering Museum displaying vintage ice axes, climbing suits, oxygen gear from the historic 1953 Everest expedition, scale models of Himalayan peaks, and Tenzing Norgay's memorial samadhi.

name: Japanese Peace Pagoda & Nipponzan Myohoji Temple
description: Established in 1972 under the guidance of Nichidatsu Fuji (founder of the Nipponzan-Myohoji Buddhist Order) on Jalapahar hill in Darjeeling, a gleaming 28.5-meter-high white stupa designed to unite people of all races in the search for world peace, featuring four large polished sandstone carvings depicting the four avatars of Lord Buddha and offering aerial views of Darjeeling and Mount Kanchenjunga.

name: Jorpokhri Wildlife Sanctuary Darjeeling
description: Perched at an elevation of 7,400 feet (2,255 meters) in Sukhiapokhri 19 km from Darjeeling, established as a specialized wildlife sanctuary across 4 hectares, centered around two pristine natural freshwater lakes ('Jor Pokhri' meaning Twin Lakes), created specifically to preserve the critically endangered Himalayan Newt / Salamander (Tylototriton verrucosus)—a living prehistoric amphibian fossil, featuring landscaped walking promenades, swans, and frontal views of Kanchenjunga.

name: Jungpana Tea Estate Kurseong
description: Situated in a dramatic, isolated mountain pocket at elevations from 3,000 to 4,500 feet near Kurseong, accessible only by crossing a narrow suspension footbridge over the roaring Jungpana mountain torrent and ascending a steep flight of stone stairs, world-renowned for producing some of the most exclusive and expensive organic second-flush Muscatel black teas in existence, savored by royal families and high-end tea blenders.

name: Kurseong
description: Kurseong, situated in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, is a charming hill station that offers a unique blend of natural beauty, adventure, and cultural heritage. With its stunning vistas of the Himalayas, lush forests, and rolling tea gardens, Kurseong is an ideal destination for trekking enthusiasts, nature lovers, and those seeking a tranquil retreat from the hustle and bustle of city life. The town has a rich history, having been a popular summer resort during the British colonial era, and its cultural landscape is influenced by the diverse communities that inhabit the region, including the Lepchas, Nepalis, and Bengalis. Visitors can explore the town's many attractions, including its historic churches, museums, and markets, and enjoy a range of outdoor activities, such as trekking, rock climbing, and bird watching.

name: Lamahatta Eco Park Darjeeling
description: Developed in 2012 by the West Bengal State Forest Department at an elevation of 5,700 feet in Lamahatta village 23 km from Darjeeling, an enchanting eco-park landscaped amidst towering Dhupi and pine trees, featuring stone garden pathways, colorful prayer flags fluttering in the mountain breeze, viewing gazebos, and a steep uphill nature trail leading to a sacred hilltop lake revered by local Buddhist monks.

name: Latpanchar & Hornbill Sanctuary Darjeeling
description: Perched at an elevation of 4,200 feet in the northernmost upper ridge of the Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary 41 km from Siliguri, celebrated internationally among ornithologists as the premier habitat in India for the globally vulnerable Rufous-necked Hornbill (Aceros nipalensis), featuring dense cinchona plantations, Raja Rani Hill viewpoint, and the sacred Ahal Dara lake.

name: Lepchajagat
description: Nestled in the heart of the Singalila National Park, Lepchajagat is a serene trekking destination that offers breathtaking views of the Himalayas. This quaint hamlet is home to the Lepcha community, a indigenous tribe known for their rich cultural heritage and expertise in traditional crafts and textiles. As you wander through the narrow trails and picturesque villages, you'll uncover the secrets of this hidden haven, where nature's splendor and adventure beckon.

name: Lopchu Tea Estate & Peda Heritage Darjeeling
description: Situated along the scenic Peshok Road connecting Darjeeling and Kalimpong at an altitude of 4,800 feet, established in the 1860s across 226 acres, internationally celebrated for its unique, rich, smoky full-bodied orthodox black tea crafted with special firing techniques, famous across Bengal for its traditional roadside confectionery producing the iconic, melt-in-the-mouth 'Lopchu Peda' sweet made of caramelized milk mawa.

name: Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary (Sukna Gateway)
description: Spanning 159 square kilometers in the foothills between the Teesta and Mahananda rivers from Sukna at 500 feet to Latpanchar at 4,000 feet, established as a sanctuary in 1976, celebrated as a crucial ecological migration corridor for wild Asian elephants, Royal Bengal tigers, Indian leopards, Himalayan black bears, and over 300 bird species, featuring open-top jeep safaris starting from Sukna station where the Darjeeling Toy Train enters the mountains.

name: Makaibari Tea Estate Kurseong
description: Established in 1859 by Captain Samler in Kurseong across 1,575 acres of pristine sub-tropical forest, celebrated globally as the very first tea factory in the world and the pioneer of organic biodynamic tea cultivation, famed for its legendary 'Silver Tips Imperial' tea harvested only on full moon nights that sold at an auction record of over USD $1,850 per kilogram, offering community homestays with tea pluckers.

name: Manebhanjan Singalila Base Camp
description: Situated at an altitude of 7,054 feet right on the international border between India and Nepal 26 km from Darjeeling, recognized worldwide as the starting base camp for the legendary Singalila Ridge trek to Sandakphu and Phalut, famous for its fleet of vintage 1950s British Series-I Land Rovers (the only motorized vehicles capable of climbing the rocky terrain), and the picturesque Chitrey Buddhist monastery trail.

name: Margaret's Hope Tea Estate Kurseong
description: Originally founded in the 1860s by British tea planter Mr. Bagdon across 580 hectares along the Hill Cart Road near Kurseong at an altitude of 6,800 feet, originally named 'Bara Ringtong' and renamed 'Margaret's Hope' in memory of the planter's beloved daughter Margaret who fell in love with the estate but tragically died during her voyage back from England, celebrated for its legendary second-flush clonal black teas and romantic mountain tea lounge.

name: Meghma Cloud Hamlet Singalila
description: Perched at an elevation of 9,514 feet (2,900 meters) on the international boundary between India and Nepal 9 km from Manebhanjan, a mystical mountain hamlet whose name literally translates to 'Mother of Clouds' ('Megh' meaning cloud), shrouded in perpetual swirling white fog, famous for the prominent Sangchen Choeling Monastery (housing 108 statues of Lord Buddha and Bodhisattvas) and a border fork where the trek path splits toward Tonglu and Tumling.

name: Mirik Lake (Sumendu Lake)
description: Nestled at an elevation of 4,905 feet in the picturesque hill town of Mirik 49 km from Darjeeling, an idyllic 1.25-kilometer-long natural freshwater lake (Sumendu Lake) fed by natural perennial streams, bordered on one side by a 3.5-km cobblestone lakeside promenade and on the other by a dense weeping pine forest (Dhupi), connected by the graceful 80-foot arched rainbow footbridge (Indreni Bridge).

name: Mungpoo (Rabindranath Tagore Memorial)
description: Situated 33 km from Darjeeling at an altitude of 3,700 feet, celebrated internationally as the premier cinchona (quinine) plantation center of India and the beloved mountain retreat of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore, who stayed at the heritage bungalow of novelist Maitreyi Devi four times between 1938 and 1940, composing his famous poem 'Camellia' and celebrating his 80th birthday here, preserved today as the Rabindra Bhavan Museum.

name: Observatory Hill & Mahakal Temple Darjeeling
description: Rising steeply above Chowrasta Mall at an elevation of 7,100 feet in Darjeeling, celebrated as the oldest sacred site in the town where the original historic Dorje-Ling Buddhist monastery once stood, housing the venerated Mahakal Cave Temple where Hindu Brahmin priests and Tibetan Buddhist lamas sit side by side chanting mantras and ringing bells amidst thousands of fluttering colorful prayer flags.

name: Orange Valley (Bloomfield) Tea Estate Darjeeling
description: Originally known as Bloomfield and established in the 1860s in the valley below Ghoom at elevations from 4,500 to 6,000 feet, celebrated for its organic, single-origin Darjeeling orthodox teas and its historic orange tree groves that gave the estate its picturesque name 'Orange Valley', featuring scenic terraced slopes facing the snow-clad peaks of Mount Kanchenjunga, mountain river streams, and guided tea-tasting sessions.

name: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park
description: Opened in 1958 across 67.5 acres at an elevation of 7,000 feet on Birch Hill in Darjeeling, recognized as the highest-altitude zoo in India and recipient of the prestigious international Earth Heroes Award, celebrated globally for its pioneer captive breeding programs for endangered alpine species including the Red Panda, Snow Leopard, Tibetan Wolf, and Himalayan Monal pheasant.

name: Phalut Peak (Singalila Ridge)
description: Rising to 3,600 meters (11,811 feet) along the Singalila Ridge 21 km beyond Sandakphu, the second highest peak in West Bengal, located at the precise tri-junction of West Bengal, Sikkim, and Nepal, known in the indigenous Lepcha language as 'Omneksha' and celebrated for offering an extraordinarily close, unhindered view of Mount Kanchenjunga's sheer south face across an open windswept plateau.

name: Rohini Mountain Viewpoint & Valley Road
description: Constructed as a modern, smooth mountain highway connecting Matigara in Siliguri directly to Kurseong across the lower Himalayan foothills, recognized as one of the most picturesque scenic mountain drives in West Bengal, climbing through the lush Rohini tea garden, offering elevated roadside viewpoints overlooking the expansive plains of North Bengal, the sparkling Balasun River bed, and cool mountain breezes.

name: Sandakphu Peak (11,930 Ft - Highest in West Bengal)
description: Perched at an elevation of 3,636 meters (11,930 feet) on the India-Nepal border along the Singalila Ridge, the highest mountain summit in West Bengal, celebrated worldwide as the only vantage point on earth where four of the world's five highest peaks (Mount Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, and Makalu) can be viewed together in a single breathtaking panorama, including the majestic 'Sleeping Buddha' formation.

name: Selim Hill Tea Estate & Nature Retreat
description: Established in 1870 by British planter Mr. Henry near Gayabari along the Hill Cart Road at an altitude of 3,500 feet, spanning 400 hectares contiguous with the dense forests of the Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary, celebrated as a model bio-diverse tea habitat, featuring an authentic 150-year-old stone planter's bungalow, the Selim Hill Tea Lounge, and the 'Tea-Canopy-Wild' conservation tracking corridor.

name: Senchal Wildlife Sanctuary & Senchal Lake
description: Established in 1915 CE across 38.6 square kilometers of prime high-altitude temperate forest at elevations ranging from 4,900 to 8,500 feet around Tiger Hill, celebrated as one of the oldest designated wildlife sanctuaries in India, covered in primeval oak, pine, and rhododendron canopies, home to barking deer, Himalayan black bears, leopards, and the historic twin Senchal Lakes constructed in 1910 and 1932 to provide pure mountain drinking water to Darjeeling.

name: Singalila National Park (Singalila Ridge)
description: Encompassing 78.6 square kilometers along the Singalila Ridge between 2,400 meters and 3,636 meters on the international border with Nepal, declared a National Park in 1992, world-famous as one of India's premier high-altitude wilderness sanctuaries preserving the endangered Red Panda, Himalayan Black Bear, Clouded Leopard, barking deer, and over 20 endemic species of wild rhododendrons and magnolias.

name: Singtom Tea Estate & Resort Darjeeling
description: Established in 1862 by German priest Father Steinthal across 1,600 acres just 20 minutes below Darjeeling town, recognized as the oldest operational tea estate resort in the world, featuring an authentic 1862 Victorian stone bungalow with century-old cedar beam ceilings, four-poster brass beds, and expansive tea gardens dropping 3,000 feet into the valley.

name: Sittong Orange Village & Ahaldhara Viewpoint
description: Nestled in the sub-tropical foothill valley of the Riyang River 35 km from Darjeeling, internationally celebrated as the 'Orange Village' of North Bengal where hundreds of terraced orchards turn vibrant golden-orange during winter harvests, famous for Ahaldhara peak (offering a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic view of Kanchenjunga and the meandering Teesta River gorge), and a 350-year-old Buddhist bamboo monastery.

name: Sonada Monastery & Balasun Valley
description: Situated at an elevation of 6,143 feet along the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway line between Kurseong and Ghum, an idyllic mountain town famous for the Samdrup Darjayling Monastery (Sonada Monastery) established in 1966 by the venerable Tibetan master Kalu Rinpoche, housing his holy preservation stupa, surrounded by the Balasun River valley, tea plantations, and fragrant pine woods.

name: Sourenee Tea Estate Mirik
description: Covering 137 hectares of rolling slopes near Mirik at an elevation of 5,000 feet, named after 'Sour' (a regional medicinal herb), celebrated as a certified organic and bio-dynamic tea garden producing sweet aromatic teas, featuring the Sourenee Tea Temple resort, horseback riding through tea bushes, and panoramic vistas of the Nepal border hills.

name: Srikhola & Gurdum Valley Darjeeling
description: Nestled in a deep, lush mountain valley at an elevation of 6,200 feet at the descent trail of the Sandakphu circuit, celebrated for the roaring Srikhola River rushing over colossal granite boulders, an iconic wooden suspension hanging bridge connecting forest cottages, dense magnolia, oak, and rhododendron woodlands, and organic cardamom farms.

name: St. Andrew's Church Darjeeling (Mall Ridge)
description: Built in 1843 and rebuilt in 1873 following lightning damage along the elevated ridge near Chowrasta Mall at 7,100 feet in Darjeeling, celebrated as the oldest Christian place of worship in Darjeeling town, designed in the early English Gothic style using local granite stones and heavy timber trusses, featuring an iconic belfry clock tower with a chiming bell cast in 1883, brass memorial plaques honoring British military officers and early tea planters, and panoramic views of Kanchenjunga.

name: Sukhiapokhri Pine Forest & Jorpokhri
description: Perched at an elevation of 7,198 feet (2,194 meters) on a high mountain ridge 11 km from Ghum, an atmospheric transit town on the border of Nepal surrounded by dense hemlock, dhupi, and pine forests, serving as the gateway to the Jorpokhri Wildlife Sanctuary (twin sacred lakes conserving the endangered Himalayan Newt / Salamander) and offering views of Kanchenjunga.

name: Takdah Heritage Cantonment & Orchid Centre
description: Situated at an elevation of 4,000 feet 28 km from Darjeeling, established in 1911 as a British colonial military cantonment for Gorkha regiments, famous for its cluster of charming century-old British stone bungalows with gabled tin roofs and fireplaces, dense cedar and pine forests shrouded in perpetual mist ('Takdah' means 'mist' in Lepcha), and one of Asia's finest government orchid cultivation breeding centers.

name: Teesta River Gorge & Coronation Bridge Sevoke
description: Situated at Sevoke 20 km northeast of Siliguri where the emerald Teesta River cuts dramatically through the Himalayan foothill gorge, celebrated for the iconic Coronation Bridge (constructed in 1941 to commemorate the coronation of King George VI, featuring a breathtaking reinforced-concrete open spandrel arch spanning 268 feet across the turbulent river gorge), and serving as the premier whitewater river rafting hub in Bengal.

name: Tenzing Rock & Gombu Rock Darjeeling
description: Situated along Lebong Cart Road 4 km from Darjeeling town, a pair of gigantic natural granite rock formations named in honor of Everest pioneer Tenzing Norgay and his nephew Nawang Gombu (the first man in the world to summit Mount Everest twice), utilized by the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute for fundamental rock-climbing and rappelling instruction, equipped with professional ropes and harnesses for public climbing trials.

name: Tiger Hill Darjeeling
description: Perched at 8,482 feet (2,590 m) altitude, the highest summit in the Darjeeling ridge, world-famous for its spectacular sunrise views where the sun illuminates the twin snow peaks of Mount Kanchenjunga in shades of gold and pink.

name: Tinchuley Village & Orange Orchards
description: Perched at an elevation of 5,800 feet near the Sikkim border 32 km from Darjeeling, an idyllic model mountain eco-village whose name 'Tinchuley' signifies 'Three Chullahs' (Three Ovens) referring to three prominent hilltops that resemble traditional clay ovens, surrounded by fragrant pine forests, tea gardens, terraced orange orchards, and the breathtaking Gumbadara viewpoint overlooking the Teesta and Rangeet river confluence.

name: Tindharia Railway Workshop & DHR Works
description: Perched at an elevation of 2,822 feet along the Hill Cart Road in Tindharia 30 km from Siliguri, established in 1915 as the dedicated heavy mechanical overhaul and repair workshop for the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, celebrated as a living temple of industrial archaeology where skilled master craftsmen hand-forge replacement parts, boiler tubes, and brass fittings for century-old B-Class steam locomotives using original British machine tools.

name: Tonglu Singalila Ridge Darjeeling
description: Perched at an elevation of 10,074 feet (3,070 meters) along the Singalila Ridge 11 km from Manebhanjan, an iconic mountain peak and trekking stopover, famous for its historic GTA trekker's hut, a natural reflection pond, and an unobstructed 360-degree panoramic vantage point overlooking the massive 'Sleeping Buddha' snow formation of Mount Kanchenjunga and the rolling hills of Nepal and Sikkim.

name: Tukvar Tea Estate Darjeeling
description: Established in 1856 by British planters in the Rangeet River valley directly below North Point, spanning 1,000 acres of fertile mountain terraces, celebrated as the lower terminal station of the iconic Darjeeling Ropeway, producing crisp floral first-flush orthodox black teas surrounded by pine forests.

name: Tumling Border Hamlet Singalila
description: Situated at an altitude of 9,600 feet (2,926 meters) along the Singalila Ridge 13 km from Manebhanjan, a picturesque mountain hamlet straddling the international boundary between India and Nepal without physical fences, famous for warm Sherpa family homestays, prayer flag-adorned stone cottages, and breathtaking sunset vistas of Mount Kanchenjunga.

name: Ananta Basudeba Terracotta Temple Bansberia
description: Constructed in 1679 CE by Raja Rameswar Datta inside the fortified royal citadel of Bansberia in Hooghly district, recognized as one of the finest and most ornately decorated terracotta temples in India, built in the traditional curved-cornice eka-ratna style topped by an octagonal shikhara, world-famous for its complete facade coverage of micro-detailed terracotta plaques illustrating the Mahabharata, Ramayana, sea vessels, and royal processions.

name: Bandel Church (Basilica of the Holy Rosary)
description: Founded in 1599 CE by Portuguese Augustinian friars on the western banks of the Hooghly River in Bandel, recognized as the oldest surviving Christian church in West Bengal, declared a Minor Basilica by Pope John Paul II in 1988, celebrated for its historic 40-foot ship mast erected in front of the church by a Portuguese sea captain in gratitude for surviving a catastrophic ocean storm, three altars, grand pipe organ, and the miraculous statue of Our Lady of Happy Voyage.

name: Chandannagar Museum & Dupleix Palace
description: Situated along the scenic Strand promenade in Chandannagar, the historic official residence of French Governor Joseph Francois Dupleix dating back to the 18th century, transformed into the Institut de Chandernagor museum and French language institute, housing an invaluable collection of French colonial furniture, bronze busts of Napoleon and Dupleix, 18th-century Anglo-French battle cannons, period maps, and French East India Company coins.

name: Danish Tavern & Serampore Heritage Hub
description: Situated on the banks of the Hooghly River 25 km north of Kolkata, celebrated as the historic commercial settlement of the Danish East India Company known as Frederiksnagore from 1755 to 1845, featuring the meticulously restored 1786 Danish Tavern by the National Museum of Denmark, St. Olav's Church built in 1806, and the magnificent neoclassical Serampore College founded in 1818 by pioneer missionary William Carey, home to Asia's first modern printing press.

name: Debanandapur Sarat Chandra Memorial Hooghly
description: Situated in Debanandapur village 4 km west of Bandel in Hooghly district, celebrated as the historic birthplace of legendary Bengali novelist and immortal storyteller Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay (1876-1938, author of 'Devdas', 'Parineeta', 'Pather Dabi', and 'Srikanta'), featuring his ancestral house, memorial museum, personal library, reading room, and the village pond where he spent his adventurous boyhood days that inspired 'Chhelebelar Dinguli'.

name: French Institute & Chandannagar Strand
description: Established in 1673 as the capital of French India on the banks of the Hooghly River 35 km from Kolkata, celebrated for its 1-km tree-lined riverfront promenade (The Strand) lined with streetlights and colonial villas, the Institut de Chandernagore (former palace of French Governor Joseph François Dupleix housing rare French antiques, canons, and Anglo-French treaties), and the 1720 CE Sacred Heart Church with French stained-glass windows.

name: Furfura Sharif Dargah Hooghly
description: Situated in Jangipara block of Hooghly district 40 km from Kolkata, celebrated as one of the most revered and influential Sufi spiritual shrines in eastern India and Bangladesh, centered around the sacred Mazar (tomb) of the 19th-century Sufi reformer and scholar Hazrat Pir Abu Bakr Siddique (known as 'Dada Huzoor Pir Qibla') and his five sons, alongside a historic 1375 CE mosque built by Sultan Muzaffar Shah.

name: Guptipara Terracotta Temple Complex Hooghly
description: Situated along the Hooghly River in Balagarh block 85 km from Kolkata, celebrated as a monumental Vaishnava temple complex founded in the 17th century, comprising four magnificent temples: Chaitanya, Brindabanchandra (1810 At-chala), Ramachandra (1678 Char-chala with stunning Ramayana terracotta carvings), and Krishnachandra, historically famous as the historic birthplace of Bengal's first public 'Barowari' (community) Durga Puja initiated in 1790 by 12 friends.

name: Hangseshwari Temple Bansberia
description: Commissioned in 1801 by Raja Nrisinghadev Roy and completed in 1814 by his widow Rani Sankari, recognized as one of India's most architecturally unique temples, featuring 13 soaring minaret-like spires (ratnas) sculpted to represent closed lotus buds, with the five-storeyed interior representing the human Kundalini yogic anatomy (Ida, Pingala, Sushumna, Chitrini, and Vajrakhya nadis), enshrining a four-armed blue neem-wood deity of Goddess Hangseshwari seated upon a thousand-petalled lotus.

name: Hooghly Imambara Chinsurah
description: Constructed between 1841 and 1861 by architect Syed Keramat Ali according to the philanthropic will of legendary Bengali humanitarian Haji Muhammad Mohsin, an imposing two-storeyed Shia congregational palace overlooking the Hooghly River, featuring a massive central clock tower rising 150 feet flanked by twin 85-foot minarets with 152 winding steps, an antique Victorian chiming clock built by Black & Murray of London, and exquisite Persian verses carved into marble walls.

name: Itachuna Rajbari (Bargee Danga)
description: Constructed in 1766 CE across sprawling grounds in Itachuna village by the Kundan family (ancestors of Maratha warriors known as 'Bargis' who settled in Bengal after the 1740s treaties), an opulent red-brick ancestral palace divided into five courtyards, featuring ornate wooden balconies, antique four-poster mahogany beds, an active family temple of Sridhar Jiu, and transformed into an award-winning royal heritage homestay.

name: Kamarpukur (Birthplace of Sri Ramakrishna)
description: Situated in Arambagh subdivision of Hooghly district 90 km from Kolkata, celebrated as the holy birthplace of 19th-century Hindu mystic saint Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa (1836-1886), guru of Swami Vivekananda and apostle of religious harmony, featuring the white marble Ramakrishna Math temple built in 1951 enshrining a marble statue of Sri Ramakrishna, his preserved ancestral thatched room, and the sacred Haldarpukur tank.

name: Mahesh Jagannath Temple Serampore
description: Established in 1396 CE by 14th-century Vaishnava sage Dhrubananda Brahmachari on the banks of the Hooghly River in Mahesh, Serampore, celebrated as the second oldest Jagannath temple and chariot procession (Rath Yatra) in the entire world after Puri, featuring colossal neem-wood deities of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra, and a monumental 50-foot, 125-tonne iron chariot with 12 massive iron wheels built in 1896 by Martin Burn.

name: Muktakeshi Navaratna Temple Sukharia Hooghly
description: Constructed in 1813 CE by the aristocratic Mustafi zamindar family in the heritage temple village of Sukharia (Balagarh block) in Hooghly district, celebrated as an architectural tour de force of late Bengal terracotta art, designed as a towering nine-pinnacled (navaratna) brick temple enshrining Goddess Kali as Muktakeshi ('She with Disheveled Hair'), adorned with hundreds of delicate terracotta plaques depicting scenes from the Ramayana, battle armadas, and European traders.

name: Sacred Heart Church Chandannagar
description: Constructed between 1875 and 1884 under French Catholic missionary Father Paul Barthet along the Strand in Chandannagar, celebrated as the architectural crown jewel of the former French colonial settlement in Bengal, designed by French architect Jacques Duchatz in the classical French Gothic revival style, featuring twin soaring front steeples, a curved semi-circular apse, and rare imported French stained-glass windows depicting the events of the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

name: Serampore College & William Carey Museum
description: Founded in 1818 along the Hooghly River in Serampore (Frederiksnagore) by the legendary Serampore Trio (William Carey, Joshua Marshman, and William Ward), incorporated in 1827 by Royal Danish Charter issued by King Frederick VI of Denmark, recognized as Asia's first degree-granting modern university, featuring a monumental neoclassical Greek Ionic facade, sweeping twin cast-iron staircases gifted by the King of Denmark, and the Carey Museum displaying the historic 1800 Gutenberg-style wooden printing press and Carey's polyglot Bible translations.

name: Tarakeswar Shiva Temple Hooghly
description: Constructed in 1729 CE by Raja Bharamalla in the traditional classic At-chala (eight-eaved) architectural style in the temple town of Tarakeswar, celebrated as the paramount Shaivite pilgrimage destination in West Bengal, enshrining a self-manifested (Swayambhu) Lingam of Lord Shiva as 'Taraknath', featuring a massive natmandir, and the adjacent holy Dudhpukur (Milk Tank) where pilgrims take a holy dip before offering sacred water.

name: Tribeni Confluence & Zafar Khan Ghazi Mosque
description: Situated at the sacred river confluence where three sacred streams (Ganga, Jamuna, and Saraswati) bifurcate—known as 'Muktaveni' (the Liberated Braid), revered for over two millennia as a paramount Hindu pilgrimage ghat, featuring the monumental 1298 CE Dargah and Mosque of Zafar Khan Ghazi built from basalt stone pillars salvaged from ancient Hindu and Buddhist temples, recognized as the oldest surviving standing Islamic building in Bengal.

name: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden
description: Historic 273-acre botanical garden founded in 1787 by Robert Kyd on the Hooghly banks, home to the Great Banyan Tree with a canopy circumference exceeding 450 meters.

name: AJC Bose Indian Botanic Garden (Shibpur Botanical Garden)
description: Established in 1787 by Lieutenant Colonel Robert Kyd on the western bank of the Hooghly River in Shibpur, Howrah, celebrated as the oldest and largest botanical garden in India spanning 273 lush acres with 12,000 living plant specimens across 25 divisions, internationally famous for the colossal 250-year-old Great Banyan Tree (Ficus benghalensis) whose aerial root canopy covers over 3.5 acres (making it the widest tree canopy on Earth), giant Victoria amazonica water lilies, and the Central National Herbarium.

name: Andul Rajbari & Annapurna Temple Howrah
description: Constructed in 1834 by Raja Rajnarayan Roy Bahadur in Andul 14 km west of Kolkata, celebrated as one of the most magnificent neoclassical zamindari palaces in Bengal, designed in grand Greco-Roman classical architecture featuring soaring Corinthian columns, sweeping marble staircases, an ornate open-air Natmandir, the sacred Annapurna temple, and an ancient brass and wooden Rath chariot procession celebrated since the 18th century.

name: Belur Math
description: Headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission founded by Swami Vivekananda on the western bank of the Hooghly, featuring unique architecture fusing Hindu, Christian, and Islamic design elements.

name: Deulti & Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay Kuthi
description: Nestled on the serene banks of the Rupnarayan River in Samtaber near Deulti 60 km from Kolkata, the picturesque ancestral-style two-storeyed Burmese-wood house (Kuthi) where legendary Bengali novelist Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay lived from 1926 until his death in 1938, where he penned timeless literary classics including 'Devdas', 'Palli Samaj', 'Srikanta', and 'Mahesh', preserved as a memorial museum surrounded by bamboo groves and clay courtyards.

name: Eastern Railway Museum
description: An open-air railway heritage museum at Foreshore Road showcasing vintage steam locomotives, royal saloons, toy trains, and historical railway equipment from the 19th and 20th centuries.

name: Gadiara & Three-River Confluence Howrah
description: Situated at the southern tip of Howrah district 80 km from Kolkata, where three mighty rivers (the Hooghly, Damodar, and Rupnarayan) merge into an immense, sea-like expanse of water, celebrated for its wide breezy riverfront promenades, dramatic sunrises and sunsets reflecting across vast waters, motorized ferry boat rides across to Geonkhali and Nurpur, and the submerged ruins of Fort Mornington built by Lord Clive in the 1760s.

name: Garchumuk & 58-Vent Sluice Gate Howrah
description: Situated at the scenic confluence of the Hooghly and Damodar rivers in Shyampur block of Howrah district 60 km from Kolkata, celebrated as one of southern Bengal's finest riverfront eco-tourism destinations, famous for the monumental 'Atanna Gate' (58-Vent Sluice Gate constructed during the British era to control tidal floodwaters), a 50-acre riverside deer park housing herds of spotted deer, children's amusement parks, and river cruises.

name: Howrah Bridge
description: Officially Rabindra Setu, the iconic balanced cantilever suspension bridge over the Hooghly River built with 26,500 tonnes of high-tensile steel without nuts or bolts.

name: Howrah Junction
description: The oldest and largest railway complex in India, with 23 platforms operating since 1854, housed in a magnificent colonial red-brick Romanesque-style terminal building.

name: Panitras Samtaber (Sarat Chandra Memorial Kuthi) Howrah
description: Situated on the peaceful banks of the Rupnarayan River at Samtaber in Panitras near Bagnan in Howrah district, the historic two-storeyed country house (Kuthi) where immortal Bengali novelist Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay resided from 1923 until shortly before his passing in 1938, featuring a traditional Burmese pagoda-style curved roof, his personal writing desk, easy chair, hookah, handwritten manuscripts, and the sacred courtyard pond and guava trees immortalized in his literature.

name: Santragachi Jheel Migratory Bird Haven
description: Spanning 32 acres near Santragachi Railway Station in Howrah, recognized as one of the most prominent urban wetland wintering sites in eastern India, attracting thousands of migratory waterfowl each winter between November and February traveling from Siberia and Ladakh, including Lesser Whistling Ducks, Ferruginous Pochards, Gadwalls, Garganeys, Northern Pintails, and Baikal Teals.

name: Uluberia Riverfront & Boat-Building Docks
description: Situated along the western bank of the Hooghly River in Howrah district 30 km from Kolkata, celebrated since the 17th century as a strategic river anchorage and crossing point where Job Charnock briefly considered founding the British capital before selecting Sutanuti, famous for its historic timber boat-building yards where traditional wooden cargo dinghies and country boats are hand-crafted, river promenades, and the sacred Kalibari temple.

name: Chalsa Hill & Kurti Tea Gardens
description: Situated at an altitude of 1,000 feet in the Himalayan foothills 60 km from Siliguri, celebrated as the picturesque gateway junction of the Western Dooars, crowned by the hilltop Chalsa view point overlooking the Kurti tea garden, the winding Murti River valley, and dense sal forests frequented by migrating elephant herds.

name: Chapramari Wildlife Sanctuary Jalpaiguri
description: Spanning 9.6 square kilometers of dense sal and moist deciduous forest on the northern banks of the Murti River contiguous with Gorumara National Park, declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1998, renowned for its central elevated watchtower overlooking a large perennial salt lick and waterhole where wild herds of Asian elephants, Indian gaurs (bison), and spotted deer gather daily.

name: Diana River Bridge & Nagrakata Foothills
description: Situated near Nagrakata along NH-31C in the Western Dooars 70 km from Siliguri, celebrated for the monumental Diana River Bridge spanning the wide, rocky, boulder-strewn bed of the turbulent Diana River where it rushes down from the southern hills of Bhutan, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the blue Himalayan foothill ridges, lush tea gardens, and migrating elephant herds.

name: Gajoldoba & Teesta Barrage (Pakhibitan Sanctuary)
description: Formed by the construction of the monumental Teesta Barrage across the emerald waters of the Teesta River in Jalpaiguri district 25 km from Siliguri, a vast aquatic reservoir surrounded by Baikunthapur forest and framed by distant snow peaks of Mount Kanchenjunga, declared as the Pakhibitan Bird Sanctuary hosting thousands of trans-Himalayan migratory birds including Ruddy Shelducks, Bar-headed Geese, and Great Crested Grebes.

name: Gorumara National Park Dooars
description: Nestled in the Dooars terai region at the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas, an 80-sq-km national park stretching along the Murti and Raidak rivers, world-famous for its thriving population of the great Indian one-horned rhinoceros, wild Asian elephants, and gaur.

name: Lataguri Forest Gate & Nature Hub
description: Situated on the outskirts of Gorumara National Park along the Malbazar highway in Jalpaiguri district, celebrated as the primary hospitality and safari gateway to Gorumara, featuring the Forest Department's Nature Interpretation Centre with life-sized wildlife dioramas, direct jeep safari booking counters for Jatraprasad and Rhino watchtowers, and tribal cultural dance open-air stages.

name: Malbazar Tea Tourism & Kumlai Park
description: Situated at the base of the Kalimpong foothills 55 km from Siliguri along NH-31, celebrated as the commercial and administrative epicenter of the Western Dooars tea industry, surrounded by dozens of sprawling tea gardens (including Raja, Good Hope, and Damdim), featuring the municipal Kumlai Nature Park, panoramic views of the Chel River basin, and vibrant weekly ethnic haats.

name: Murti Tourist Complex & Riverbed Jalpaiguri
description: Situated on the crystal-clear, pebble-strewn banks of the Murti River where it emerges from the Himalayan foothills between Gorumara National Park and Chapramari Wildlife Sanctuary, celebrated as the scenic recreational epicenter of the Western Dooars, featuring the WBTDCL Murti Tourist Lodge, gentle shallow riverbeds where wild elephants bathe, and forest suspension bridges.

name: Samsing Village
description: Samsing Village is a picturesque destination located in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, known for its lush green forests, rolling hills, and stunning views of the Himalayas. The village is situated at an altitude of 3000 feet above sea level and is surrounded by dense forests of oak, birch, and pine trees, making it a perfect getaway for nature lovers and photographers. With its tranquil atmosphere, Samsing Village offers a unique opportunity to experience the traditional rural life of West Bengal and connect with nature. The village has a rich cultural heritage, with a mix of Nepali, Bengali, and tribal influences, which is reflected in its architecture, cuisine, and festivals.

name: Belpahari & Ghagra Waterfalls Jhargram
description: Situated 45 km northwest of Jhargram in the rugged forest hills bordering Jharkhand, celebrated as the scenic eco-tourism heart of Jhargram district, famous for the breathtaking Ghagra Waterfalls (where the rushing waters of the Tarapheni river carve bizarre geological potholes, caves, and swirling channels through solid black canyon rocks), Tarafeni Barrage, and dense Sal, Mahua, and Kendu woodlands.

name: Belpahari Forest Ranges & Tribal Trails
description: Sprawling across the western hilly highlands of Jhargram district 45 km from Jhargram town, celebrated as a rugged paradise of forest hills, undulating laterite plateaus, and dense Sal and Mahua woodlands stretching to the border of Jharkhand, featuring scenic hiking trails through rocky escarpments, pristine Santhal and Munda tribal hamlets painted with folk murals, natural streams, and peaceful forest rest houses.

name: Hatibari & Subarnarekha River Gorge Jhargram
description: Situated at the scenic tri-junction border point of West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand 62 km from Jhargram town, celebrated as one of the most picturesque natural river landscapes in the state, where the golden waters of the Subarnarekha River rush through a dramatic rocky gorge flanked by dense, pristine Sal and Mahua forests, offering white sandy river beaches, rocky outcrops, and quiet forest rest houses.

name: Jhargram Royal Palace & Chilkigarh
description: Constructed in the late 16th century by Sarveshwar Singh Bhanj Deo (founder of the Malladev dynasty) and expanded in 1931 across 30 sprawling acres in Jhargram, an imposing royal palace combining Italian Gothic, neoclassical, and Islamic architectural elements with grand domes and manicured lawns, alongside the nearby 18th-century Chilkigarh Palace and Kanak Durga Temple situated in a biodiverse sacred medicinal forest grove along the Dulung River.

name: Jhilli Lake Wetland & Migratory Bird Haven Jhargram
description: Situated in Gopiballavpur block 48 km from Jhargram town near the Subarnarekha River, an expansive natural freshwater wetland and reservoir surrounded by dense sal and eucalyptus plantations, celebrated as an avian paradise that hosts thousands of migratory winter waterfowl between November and February, including Lesser Whistling Ducks, Northern Pintails, Cotton Pygmy-geese, and purple swamphens, equipped with watchtowers and paddle boating.

name: Kanak Durga Temple Chilkigarh Jhargram
description: Situated deep inside a sacred medicinal botanical forest along the rocky banks of the Dulung River at Chilkigarh 14 km from Jhargram town, celebrated as the centuries-old royal sanctuary of the Dhalbhum rajas, enshrining the divine 'Kanak Durga'—a four-armed deity cast from sacred eight-metal alloy (Ashtadhatu) riding upon a golden lion, surrounded by 60 acres of untouched biodiversity forest containing over 400 species of rare medicinal herbs, and the adjacent 18th-century Chilkigarh Rajbari palace.

name: Kankrajhore Sal Forest & Mayurjharna
description: Situated at an elevation of 900 feet in the southernmost fringe of the Dalma hills 65 km from Jhargram, an exceptionally pristine wilderness hamlet whose name translates to 'Valley of Crabs and Rushing Brooks', surrounded by undulating hill ranges blanketed in dense virgin Sal, Pial, Teak, and Mahua forests, forming a core part of the Mayurjharna Elephant Reserve.

name: Kendua Migratory Bird Haven Jhargram
description: Situated 8 km from Jhargram town along the road to Chilkigarh, an extraordinary eco-village that transforms annually into one of Bengal's largest avian breeding colonies, where between June and November over 10,000 migratory Asian Openbill Storks (Anastomus oscitans), egrets, and cormorants arrive to nest and hatch their chicks across hundreds of village tamarind, peepal, and eucalyptus trees, protected fiercely by the local villagers.

name: Laljal Cave & Prehistoric Site Belpahari
description: Nestled in a remote forested valley among the rocky Belpahari hills 19 km northwest of Belpahari in Jhargram district, an extraordinary archaeological site celebrated for its prehistoric natural rock cave and the sacred spring of 'Laljal' ('Red Water', colored by natural iron minerals), where archaeological excavations by the ASI and state archaeologists yielded 5,000-year-old Stone Age microlithic tools, animal bone fragments, and ancient pottery.

name: Charkhole Himalayan Hamlet Kalimpong
description: Perched on a quiet forested mountain ridge at an elevation of 5,500 feet (1,676 meters) in Kalimpong district 30 km from Kalimpong town, celebrated as one of the most serene and unspoiled eco-tourism villages in North Bengal, enveloped in dense virgin pine, oak, and blooming rhododendron forests, offering sensational unobstructed direct views of Mount Kanchenjunga and Mount Pandim, chirping birds, and tranquil mountain homestays.

name: Chuikhim Mountain Eco-Village Kalimpong
description: Nestled at an elevation of 3,500 feet in the southern Kalimpong hills overlooking the Leesh River valley, an exceptionally tranquil and unspoiled mountain hamlet of 250 wooden-and-clay households, free from commercial hotel construction, celebrated for its babbling mountain brooks, organic cardamom and orange plantations, over 100 species of colorful Himalayan birds, and authentic home-cooked Nepali village hospitality.

name: Damsang Fort Ruins Pedong Kalimpong
